newsitem.title: CANADA: Pulp and paper price declines hurt Avenor.
newsitem.headline: Pulp and paper price declines hurt Avenor.

text.p: Sharp declines in prices for pulp and paper products turned profits at Avenor Inc into losses in its latest fourth quarter, the company said.

Avenor reported a fourth-quarter loss of C$19.1 million, or C$0.29 a share on sales of C$500.8 million, compared with a net profit a year earlier, after a C$24.8 million charge, of C$116.9 million or C$1.61 a share on sales of C$654.9 million.
"Poor market conditions in the pulp and paper sectors caused net prices to decline by 38 percent, resulting in lower operating earnings compared to the same quarter of last year," the company said.

In a statement, Paul Gagne, president and chief executive, said pulp and paper markets are expected to improve in North America during the second quarter of 1997, while offshore markets will remain suppressed until excess capacity is reduced.

Avenor said U.S. newsprint prices dropped about 12 percent in the latest fourth quarter and price erosion continued in overseas markets. North American newsprint markets are expected to improve in 1997 as consumers rebuild inventory and consumption improves modestly. Overseas prices are expected to remain below North American levels, the company said.
Avenor said it has scheduled a price increase for newsprint of US$75 a tonne for March 1 in North America.
In the pulp sector, European and North American demand was stable, but demand in Japan and other Asian markets declined sharply. As a result, the October 1 price increase was cancelled on November 1.

A recovery in pulp prices is unlikely until after the first quarter of 1997, mainly because high paper inventories are suppressing demand in the Far East markets, Avenor said. North American and European markets for pulp are expected to remain stable through the first quarter, it said.

Avenor said demand for white paper remained weak in the fourth quarter as inventories continued to be drawn down. Price increases of US$40 to US$60 a tonne announced in September deteriorated by December, it said.

Market conditions were expected to remain weak until midway through the first quarter of 1997, when the combination of sustained economic activity, lower inventories and high printer backlogs would result in improved mill operating rates and stable prices, Avenor said. The company announced a price increase of US$40 a short ton on January 6 for cutsize paper and offset rolls.

Avenor said U.S. lumber prices were expected to be above average as Canadian lumber producers managed their shipments to remain with their total annual quote allocation ending March 31. Demand and prices in the Japanese lumber market were expected to stay strong through the first two quarters of 1997, the company said.
